findings.title: MCP projection discards explicit failure and structured results

evidence.detail: Only result.content is mapped; isError, structuredContent, metadata and annotations are not returned.
The MCP branch returns the projected array as ordinary output; only thrown errors enter errorMessage conversion.
The projected content becomes the tool_result event and subsequent model history.

findings.trigger: An MCP server returns isError:true (including empty content), or returns useful structuredContent with content:[] or a lossy text summary.
findings.consequence: The model/host loses the authoritative failure flag and structured observation. An empty error or structured-only observation becomes []. A mutation confirmation available only in structuredContent cannot be inspected.
findings.suggestedFix: Carry a versioned MCP result envelope with isError, structuredContent, original content/provenance and supported annotations into the shared tool outcome. Translate failure into explicit typed error state without discarding original content. Encode text resources as text or valid media data.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Inject empty isError, misleading-text isError, structured-only, mixed text/media, text resource and resource-link results through the actual MCP→SDK→runtime path; assert authoritative fields survive, failure never becomes an empty successful observation, and resources preserve meaning.
findings.inferenceBoundary: Projection loss is directly executed in a source VM. No external server or real mutating effect was called; downstream recovery impact follows the statically traced consumer.

findings.title: MCP origin semantics change across JSON and supervised boundaries

evidence.detail: Origins live only in an object-identity WeakMap; unknown objects resolve client.
Host MCP records are merged into the resolved agent template in returned session state.
After parsing, surviving config marks propagate; remaining local/bundled template configs are blanket-marked project.
previousRun is documented as JSON state for conversation continuation.
Each main prompt assembles templates through that provenance-restoration branch.
Supervised spawn serializes templates without per-MCP provenance.
MCP discovery forwards a generic object rehydration to the parent dep; no config origin is restored.

findings.trigger: Attach a client-marked MCP descriptor to a trusted local/bundled agent, serialize the RunState, then continue from JSON; separately, use a project/user-marked MCP descriptor from a supervised child.
findings.consequence: JSON restoration of the mixed trusted template changes the peer descriptor from client to project, re-enabling local environment substitution and removing the first-call peer approval/description treatment. The supervised direction changes trusted local descriptors to unmarked/client, leaving $VAR literal and potentially breaking legitimate authentication or requiring unexpected approval.
findings.suggestedFix: Bind per-server origin to parent-owned descriptor identity/version and transport an opaque reference or authenticated provenance receipt. Restore that reference across saved runs and reverse RPC; do not infer every contained descriptor origin from template executionSource or accept self-asserted peer origin fields.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Round-trip a trusted template containing separately marked project/user/client descriptors through saved RunState and actual supervisor RPC. Assert no client descriptor upgrades, legitimate trusted substitutions survive using synthetic environment values, and unknown/forged references remain client.
findings.inferenceBoundary: The exact registry and parent-bridge helpers reproduce both origin changes. No secret value was read/expanded and no outbound endpoint contacted. Security consequence is conditional on the documented JSON continuation plus a descriptor containing environment references.

findings.title: Opted-in agent discovery imports auxiliary executable files before validating definitions

evidence.detail: Recursive entrypoint walk skips only directory skills, declaration .d.ts and suffix .test.ts.
Dynamic import occurs before checking default export/id/model or validating an agent.
Import errors are only logged when verbose; validate:true does not return them in validationErrors.
Real CLI trust option invokes this loader with validate:true and verbose:false.

findings.trigger: The user explicitly trusts project/parent agent roots, passes agentsPath, or has auxiliary .js/.ts/.mjs/.cjs/.tsx code under the trusted home .agents root; that root contains sessions, probes, tests, lib/types or node_modules.
findings.consequence: Data/probe/dependency/test modules execute as discovery entrypoints even if they export no agent. Side effects can occur during reload and discovery work grows with artifacts/dependencies. A throwing agent silently disappears while the validation diagnostics array remains empty. This is conditional on an already trusted root, not unconsented project execution.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate agent entrypoints from auxiliary code using declared manifests or narrow discovery roots. Exclude sessions/probes/tests/node_modules/types/lib from automatic entrypoint enumeration while retaining explicitly imported agent dependencies. Return directory/import/definition diagnostics independently of verbose logging.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Use the actual loader with an explicit temp agentsPath containing one valid agent and side-effect markers in every auxiliary directory and test suffix variant. Assert only declared agent entrypoints execute, imported dependencies still work, and throwing/import-invalid agents produce structured diagnostics.
findings.inferenceBoundary: The real loader imported six synthetic auxiliary files with harmless global-array markers and returned validationErrors:[] for a throwing module. The real repository .agents tree was never imported.

findings.title: Production MCP discovery stops at the first page and keeps successful listings stale

evidence.detail: Production discovery calls listMCPTools without cursor and consumes only tools; nextCursor is discarded.
Successful list promises remain cached per client+arguments; only rejected entries are removed here.
Dispatch rediscovers through the same cached listing, so this refresh does not obtain current tools.

findings.trigger: A connected server paginates tools/list or changes/removes/adds tool descriptors during its lifetime.
findings.consequence: Later-page tools are undiscoverable even when explicitly selected; removed/changed tools retain stale descriptors and new tools stay unavailable. The fast cache silently becomes the capability authority. Client eviction/close is a separate pair09 issue.
findings.suggestedFix: Collect bounded pages with repeated-cursor detection; expose incomplete listings explicitly. Maintain a server generation and invalidate listings on tools/list_changed, reconnect and explicit refresh, using a bounded fallback freshness policy when notifications are unavailable.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Fake a two-page server with a second-page selected tool, then change/remove/add tools and emit list_changed. Verify complete discovery and generation refresh with finite repeated-cursor/error/cancel behavior and healthy-server partial loading preserved.

new Function materializes the text in global scope.

findings.trigger: A valid trusted TypeScript/JavaScript generator refers to a module constant, imported helper or captured factory variable.

findings.suggestedFix: Preserve trusted host module/function references for the in-process path and produce real dependency bundles with content/version identity for binary/process transport. Keep programmaticConfig for explicit data injection; diagnose unsupported serialization during loading until bundling lands.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Load a generator importing a helper and capturing a factory setting. Run it from source, packaged binary and supervised process with identical yielded result; assert startup catches missing bundle dependencies and no inline helper duplication is required.

findings.title: Schema transport/coercion can silently broaden extension validation

evidence.detail: Invalid, degraded or unrepresentable members become native permissive schemas without an outcome field.
Fallback object is loose; integer fallback is z.number without integer enforcement.
Transport uses unrepresentable:any and eventually a generic object fallback.
Custom/MCP local validation converts JSON Schema with the same converter.
Local custom validation only checks safeParse success; parsed/coerced result is discarded and original input is forwarded.

findings.trigger: A schema becomes a serialized Zod husk, uses not/never or unsupported composite constraints, or contains additionalProperties:false.
findings.consequence: A required-object schema can accept {}, a never schema can accept an object after transport, and additionalProperties:false succeeds on extra fields. The host/model sees no explicit validation-degraded state, so schema conformance becomes unreliable across extension/process boundaries.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain canonical JSON Schema semantics with a faithful validator or authenticated parent schema authority. Return explicit unsupported/degraded validation capability when a shape cannot be preserved. Keep SDK original Zod execution checks for callbacks; preserve transport scheduling parameters outside the validated user input.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Compare original and transported acceptance matrices for required, additionalProperties, enum, integer, not/never, refs and composites. Invalid values must remain invalid or cause an explicit unsupported contract; never silently broaden. Verify SDK default/async/transform tests still pass.
findings.inferenceBoundary: These are executed helper round trips. Rich required and enum constraints did survive; loss is shape-specific, not a claim that every schema is discarded.

findings.title: Prompt-schema validation rejects valid constrained strings by testing one sentinel

evidence.detail: Validity is inferred from safeParse("test") or safeParse(undefined), not the schema accepted type.
The prompt definition uses a loose object and permits additional JSON Schema constraints.

findings.trigger: Define a string prompt schema with minLength:5, enum:["work"] or a pattern/literal that excludes "test".
findings.consequence: A schema that accepts legitimate string prompts is rejected during agent loading and the agent is unavailable.
findings.suggestedFix: Check the supported JSON Schema type/union contract structurally; validate each actual prompt at invocation. Do not use acceptance of a specific sample as a type proof.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Load minLength, enum and pattern prompt schemas excluding "test"; legitimate prompts must run while invalid invocation values are rejected with their specific constraint.

findings.title: Custom/MCP arguments are blanket-classified as filesystem paths

evidence.detail: Every collected string in arbitrary extension input is normalized as a path and can block the call.
The check runs unconditionally when a project root exists, before tool_call publication.
A leading slash means absolute filesystem path regardless of argument semantics.

findings.trigger: Call an otherwise granted API/text tool with {route:"/api/v1"}, separator:"/", a slash-delimited regex or another ordinary absolute-looking string.
findings.consequence: The body refuses legitimate tool data as a project escape. Recovery cannot use the same semantically valid input. The source calls false positives an accepted tradeoff, but the impact is an extension interoperability limitation, not a hypothetical security restriction request.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply filesystem containment to declared path/effect fields and the authoritative handler, using explicit extension capability metadata. Treat other arguments as data. Preserve current real project-path authority and intentional full-access terminal policy.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Run a non-filesystem fake tool with route, separator and regex inputs through actual dispatch; it should receive exact values. A declared filesystem tool must still refuse a real outside-project target.

findings.title: Delimiter-based extension names do not round-trip through dispatch

evidence.detail: Internal published name is server + "__" + tool with no reversible encoding.
Any custom name containing "__" is decoded as MCP; server lookup uses the first segment.
Server keys accept arbitrary strings and do not reject the internal delimiter.
Custom names are open strings; helper only prevents native names at type level.

findings.trigger: Configure server team__api with tool read, or register an ordinary SDK custom tool whose name contains __.
findings.consequence: team__api__read is decoded as server team/tool api__read, while __ custom names are routed to the wrong handler. A granted descriptor can be visible but not callable with its advertised identity.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep an explicit descriptor-id→server/tool mapping with reversible provider-safe IDs. Validate supported public names consistently and use descriptor kind instead of separator presence to distinguish MCP from SDK custom tools.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Round-trip server/tool/custom names containing __, slash and provider-incompatible characters through discovery and invocation; assert the exact intended descriptor/handler is called or a clear load-time unsupported-name error occurs.

findings.title: CLI wrapper permission receipts report a profile the producer overrides

evidence.detail: Wrapper template declares tmux-test.
Result permissionProfile is restricted to tmux-test and described as runtime-enforced.
Model is instructed to emit tmux-test as the enforced runtime profile.
Actual shared producer deliberately stamps every agent terminal call full-access.

findings.trigger: Execute any of the repository-local CLI wrapper templates through the normal model or generator terminal producer.
findings.consequence: Its structured result claims tmux-test enforcement although Openbuff terminal dispatch uses full-access. Host decisions based on that evidence receive inaccurate capability state. External CLI process flags are separate and are not proof of the Openbuff parent policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Derive effective profile/capabilities from the runtime dispatch receipt and carry them into wrapper results; make the schema accept the real configured posture. Preserve the explicitly intended full-access policy.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Feed an actual runtime-produced terminal receipt into each wrapper completion path; assert the reported effective profile matches the producer, including template/profile override cases.
findings.inferenceBoundary: Policy behavior was verified with pair09 source evidence and exact local read. No external CLI was started; this finding concerns receipt truth, not a policy bypass.

findings.title: Agent documentation promises an isolation boundary that is absent

evidence.detail: Documentation says programmatic generators execute in a secure sandbox.
Trusted strings execute via host-realm new Function, with raw agentState supplied during initialization.
Existing test deliberately documents host-global visibility, not sandbox isolation.
Remote executable templates are refused rather than run in an isolate.

findings.trigger: A user relies on the agents guide to assess the authority of a locally installed programmatic extension.
findings.consequence: Tool-yield grants are mistaken for general code isolation. Trusted extensions can use host APIs directly; no callable untrusted QuickJS/VM agent tier was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Document trusted host execution, explicit local trust opt-in and refused remote executable templates accurately. Describe any future untrusted isolation tier separately; do not restrict intentional first-party host access.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Compare published capability/help/docs with host-global test and remote provenance refusal. Current trusted execution must be described as host realm and optional unavailable isolate capability must remain false.
findings.inferenceBoundary: Trusted host execution is intentional and is not itself a runtime defect. This is a documentation mismatch; no escape probe was run.

domainAssessment.security: Explicit local/project opt-in, client origin sidecar/no-upgrade, own-key grants, protocol-peer marking and remote executable refusal are present. Conditional origin upgrade after JSON restore (10-F2) and auxiliary discovery execution inside already trusted roots (10-F3) are evidenced. Trusted first-party host/full-access policy is intentional, not a defect; secure-sandbox documentation is inaccurate (10-F11). No external exploit or credential value inspected.
domainAssessment.correctness: MCP metadata/content fidelity, dynamic discovery, descriptor naming, arbitrary-data classification, generator module closures, schema semantics and prompt sentinel rejection have concrete current triggers and bounded reproductions. Core custom Zod execution and MCP server dispatch are real working strengths.
domainAssessment.state-mutation: Origin identity cannot survive JSON; generation/root/cwd registry load ownership and derived-cache epoch bumps are sound static strengths. Aux modules mutate host state at discovery; MCP listings stay stale after first successful response. MCP eviction/close and durable replay were left to pair09/pair05.
domainAssessment.error-handling: Per-server allSettled isolates failures, list rejection deletes cache, custom-handler failure results settle and MCP server unknown/throwing paths are implemented. isError is lost in client projection; import errors disappear at validate:true/verbose:false; schema degradation is not part of authoritative result state. General retries/timeouts reviewed by responsible pairs.
domainAssessment.performance: Concurrent MCP loading and promise-cache reuse reduce redundant work; scanner caps depth 6/string count 1000. Recursive serial import of sessions/dependencies increases cold reload work and Date.now cache-busting can retain distinct modules. No latency/memory/throughput measurement was claimed. Cache freshness requires repair while keeping bounded work.
domainAssessment.dependency-hygiene: MCP/ACP/Zod and conversion ownership inspected in sdk/common manifests; common Zod and converter exact versions while MCP/ACP semver ranges exist. Notion package selector is pinned. QuickJS dependency is not evidence of an imported isolate implementation; Rust plugin-host explicitly not_implemented. No CVE/network/package-install checks; broad release/provenance remains pair11.
domainAssessment.test-coverage: Existing origin/default/refinement/cancel/schema/grant and linked-MCP server tests were read, not rerun. Fresh pinned-Bun probes used exact isolated source/helper/loader boundaries; no provider/server/CLI/model live tasks. Wrapper workspace test only asserts true; absent JSON-origin roundtrip, paginated/dynamic listing, metadata/error fidelity, auxiliary-import diagnostics and schema-acceptance equivalence coverage is material.
domainAssessment.api-contract: Open names and function-typed generators meet ambiguous-delimiter/stringification limitations; JSON schemas keep provider constraints but can lose execution validation semantics. Result/profile/isolation claims differ from effective behavior. MCP public handle narrowing has an explicit migration note; ext-v1 method schemas and honest disabled native role are positive boundaries. Foreign SDK/plugin promises are classified absent, not usable.
